study_type_evidence.quote: At t = 0 min, the mice received 25 nmol/kg BW GIP through either intravenous (IV), SC or intraperitoneal (IP) injection.
study_type_evidence.section: METHODS (Exogenous GIP injection in conscious mice)

study_type_evidence.quote: Mouse GIP(1-42) was dissolved to reach concentrations of 0, 25 and 400 pM in PBS, mouse heparin-plasma ... mouse EDTA plasma and assay buffer
We tested accuracy of the three ELISA kits in EDTA plasma, Heparin plasma, ELISA kit assay buffer and PBS.

in_vivo_species.quote: Female C57Bl/6Jrj mice (12 weeks old) were obtained from Janvier Labs (Saint Berthevin Cedex, France)

ex_vivo_detail: Mouse EDTA plasma and commercial mouse heparin plasma were spiked with GIP(1-42) at 0, 25 and 400 pM and assayed with three ELISA kits to test recovery. Mouse EDTA plasma was obtained from 5-h fasted C57Bl/6Jrj mice. Per protocol, spiking plasma removed from an animal is ex vivo; the paper labels this section 'in vitro'.
in_vitro_detail: The same spiking/recovery experiment performed in PBS and in kit assay buffer (cell-free media) is in vitro.

agents.name: mouse GIP(1-42)
agents.sequence_source: Body states only 'Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) is a 42-amino acid polypeptide hormone'; no one-letter sequence is printed in the body
agents.chemical_identifier: Synthetic mouse GIP(1-42) from Caslo peptides (Lyngby, Denmark); purity 98.03%, molecular weight confirmed by mass spectrometry
agents.group_n_quote: Mice (n = 6-9) were weighed and tail marked, and then fasted from 0800 h to 1300 h with access to water.
agents.route: intravenous, subcutaneous and intraperitoneal (half-life determined from the intravenous arm)
agents.dose_route_quote: At t = 0 min, the mice received 25 nmol/kg BW GIP through either intravenous (IV), SC or intraperitoneal (IP) injection.
agents.half_life: 93 ± 2 s (apparent half-life of intact GIP(1-42) after IV injection, without DPP-4 inhibitor)
agents.pk_quote: We estimated the apparent half-life of intact GIP(1-42) to be 93 ± 2 s, which was extended to an apparent half-life of 5 ± 0.6 min by co-administration of Val-Pyr
agents.pk_section: RESULTS (Pharmacokinetics of exogenous mouse GIP(1-42) in mice)

agents.name: valine-pyrrolidide (Val-Pyr), DPP-4 inhibitor
agents.chemical_identifier: valine-pyrrolidide (Val-Pyr), a gift from Novo Nordisk, Bagsvaerd, Denmark
agents.group_n_quote: Data are presented as mean ± SE, n = 6-9.
agents.dose_route_quote: mice received either 1) subcutaneous (SC) injection with 1.5 mg valine-pyrrolidide (Val-Pyr) ... in 50 u L 40 % 0.9 % NaCl + 60 % 0.04 mM phosphate buffer
agents.pk_quote: No pharmacokinetics were measured for Val-Pyr itself; it was co-administered and extended the apparent half-life of intact GIP(1-42) from 93 ± 2 s to 5 ± 0.6 min
agents.pk_section: RESULTS (Pharmacokinetics of exogenous mouse GIP(1-42) in mice)

agents.name: vehicle for Val-Pyr (40% 0.9% NaCl + 60% 0.04 mM phosphate buffer)
agents.group_n_quote: Data are presented as mean ± SE, n = 6-9.
agents.dose_route_quote: or 2) a SC injection with vehicle

agents.name: 0.9% NaCl with 0.1% casein (GIP dissolution vehicle)
agents.chemical_identifier: casein solution from bovine milk - 5% in water, Sigma Aldrich
agents.route: vehicle in which GIP was dissolved for injection
agents.dose_route_quote: The peptide was dissolved in 0.9 % NaCl containing 0.1 % casein

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Measurements after (A), intravenous injection, (C), subcutaneous injection and (E), intraperitoneal injection of 25 nmol/kg BW exogenous mouse GIP (1-42)
concentration_time_figure.note: Fig. 1A/C/E plot plasma total and intact GIP concentration against time (t = 0-20/30 min) after IV, SC and IP dosing with and without Val-Pyr. Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 re-plot the same plasma concentration-time data comparing RIA against commercial ELISA kits.

bioanalytical_method: In-house radioimmunoassays (RIA) for total GIP (C-terminal antiserum code no. 80,867) and intact GIP (N-terminal antiserum code no. 98,171); commercial ELISA kits (Millipore Rat/Mouse GIP total EZRMGIP-55K; Crystal Chem Mouse Active GIP 81511; Crystal Chem Mouse GIP 81517) used for comparison
bioanalytical_quote: Total and intact GIP were measured by in-house radioimmunoassays (RIAs). Total GIP was measured using an antibody that targets the free C-terminal part of the hormone (code no 80,867)
notes: The half-life is reported as an 'apparent half-life' with no kinetic phase named, so half_life_phase is 'unspecified'; the authors computed it themselves from the log-linear fall between t = 1 and t = 10 min using k = (ln(Ct1)-ln(Ct2))/Δt and t½ = ln(2)/k, which is the paper's own stated calculation. No Cmax or tmax values are reported numerically anywhere in the body; peaks are described only as percentage ratios of intact to total GIP (e.g. intact reached 41% of total after IV). AUC is reported only as incremental AUC fold-changes (IV 5.4-fold, SC 8.1-fold, IP 7.8-fold increase with Val-Pyr) and as intact-iAUC expressed as a percentage of total-iAUC (IV placebo 13 ± 1% vs Val-Pyr 74 ± 3%); no absolute AUC with units is given, so auc is 'not reported'. Other PK parameters reported in the body: clearance 207 ± 16 μL/min/g (placebo) vs 45 ± 4 μL/min/g (Val-Pyr); apparent volume of distribution 0.34 ± 0.1 mL/g vs 0.46 ± 0.03 mL/g. The Methods list blood sampling at t = 0, 1, 3, 5, 10 and 20 min but the Results refer to timepoints up to t = 30 min; both recorded as printed. Sequence of GIP(1-42) is not printed in the body.
